$comment: PCI DSS v4.0.1 → SOC 2 TSC 2017 (rev. 2022) mappings. Written from requirement intent (original paraphrases). PCI controls are CDE-scoped and prescriptive; SOC 2 criteria are entity-level outcomes, so 'partial' dominates — PCI evidence usually satisfies the criterion for the payment environment and needs widening for the full SOC 2 system boundary.
source: PCI DSS v4.0.1 requirement-intent cross-walk to AICPA TSC 2017 (rev. 2022)

mappings.rationale: Restricting inbound CDE traffic defends the system boundary against external threats.
Controls between trusted and untrusted networks are boundary-protection measures.
Hardening standards give configuration-monitoring a baseline to detect deviations from.
Purging account data at end of retention is disposal of confidential information.
PAN masking restricts logical visibility of protected data to authorized roles.
Rendering stored PAN unreadable protects data at rest within the logical-access architecture.
Strong cryptography for PAN in transit restricts information during transmission and movement.
Both require controls that prevent or detect malicious software.
Ongoing scans/behavioural analysis operate the malware-prevention control.
A secure SDLC governs how system changes are designed, tested and approved.
Identifying and risk-ranking new vulnerabilities feeds vulnerability monitoring.
Time-bound patching remediates the vulnerabilities monitoring detects.
Both require authorized, documented change management for production.
A need-to-know access model governs how access is authorized and modified.
Least-privilege assignment constrains access to roles' requirements.
Semi-annual access reviews validate that granted access remains appropriate.
Unique user IDs are foundational to logical access security.
Exception-only shared accounts preserve individual accountability in the access architecture.
Immediate revocation at termination deregisters credentials no longer authorized.
MFA for all CDE access strengthens authentication in the logical-access architecture.
MFA on remote access protects entry points from outside the system boundary.
Facility entry controls restrict physical access to protected information assets.
Destroying media containing cardholder data completes secure disposal.
Required audit-event capture produces the records incident monitoring relies on.
Daily automated review of security logs is how incidents are identified.
Detecting failures of security-control systems keeps the monitoring function trustworthy.
Quarterly internal scans detect vulnerabilities and configuration drift.
Quarterly ASV scans extend vulnerability detection to the external footprint.
Penetration testing is a separate evaluation of control effectiveness.
IDS/IPS provides the intrusion telemetry that security monitoring consumes.
File-integrity monitoring detects unauthorized configuration and content changes.
The published security policy deploys control expectations through policies and procedures.
Targeted risk analyses identify and analyse risk to set control frequency.
On-hire and annual security training communicates responsibilities internally.
Pre-hire screening supports the commitment to competent, trustworthy personnel.
The TPSP inventory is the foundation of vendor risk management.
Annual TPSP compliance monitoring manages ongoing vendor risk.
The incident response plan defines response and notification to affected parties.
Annual IR testing with lessons learned drives remediation and improvement.
